QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_30

question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the MAXIMUM leverage permitted for a Category III AIF?

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI permits Cat III AIFs to take leverage up to 2x the fund's NAV, subject to PPM disclosure, investor consent, risk-management policy, and monthly reporting to SEBI when leverage is used. The Trap: Zero is Cat I/II rule (XIX-D primary). 1x is too restrictive; 5x exceeds cap. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II) tests zero-leverage rule; XIX-E tests 2x Cat III cap — a top-10 XIX-E fact. Manager's Pro-Tip: 2x is a GROSS leverage cap. Manage margin utilisation at the PRIME BROKER (not fund admin records) — broker-held securities can be rehypothecated, creating leverage beyond official reporting if you don't segregate.
